web.meta.title: Flect - All-in-one file editor that lives in Explorer
web.meta.desc: Right-click any file or folder in Windows Explorer to convert, compress, resize, analyze, run OCR, or remove duplicate images, videos, audio, and PDFs - everything finishes right there.
web.og.title: Flect - All-in-one tools with a right click
web.og.desc: From Explorer: convert, compress, resize, analyze, OCR, and dedupe images, videos, audio, and PDFs. All in a single right click.
web.hero.title:
One right
click for
Everything
web.hero.lead:
No more hunting for converter websites in your browser, or squeezing videos in a dedicated editor.
Just right-click a file in Explorer to convert, compress, resize, analyze, run OCR, or remove duplicates...
Every task finishes right inside Explorer.
web.demo.title: Try the Demo
web.demo.desc:
Right-click a file or folder on this desktop and open Flect from the menu.
To rename, select an item and press F2, or click its name once more.
web.desk.title: Desktop
web.desk.tip: Drag across empty space to select several items, or use Ctrl / Shift + click. Press Esc to close the menu.
web.philo.line:
The time spent hunting for a converter,
and the hassle of hopping between windows.
One right click eliminates both.
web.philo.sub: Flect is a native Windows app that integrates into Explorer as a shell extension. Built with C++ / .NET, it edits files locally, so nothing is ever sent to a server.
web.pillar.safe.d: Results are always written out as new files - nothing is overwritten or deleted. If a name is already taken, a suffix like "(1)" is added.
web.pillar.batch.d: Select hundreds of files at once. The whole selection is handled in a single run - no manual, one-by-one work.
web.pillar.offline.d: All external dependencies are downloaded automatically by the installer. No uploads, no log collection - your files never leave your PC.
web.features.title: The Right Menu, Wherever You Need It
web.features.desc: For every file type, only the operations it actually needs show up in the right-click menu. Analyze on a single file follows the contents, so a renamed or spoofed extension still shows what the file really is.
web.feat.img.title: Images: From Resizing to Background Removal
web.feat.img.1: Resize - by ratio or exact pixels, with preset sizes selectable in one click from the menu.
web.feat.img.2: Compress - down to a target size while keeping quality as high as possible.
web.feat.img.3: Rotate - to any angle. Corners become transparent, or are filled with a chosen color for formats without alpha.
web.feat.img.4: Convert - between PNG, JPG, WEBP, HEIC, ICO, GIF, and SVG.
web.feat.img.5: OCR - extract text from images, then save or copy it.
web.feat.img.6: Metadata removal - strip EXIF, GPS location, comments, and camera info for safe sharing on social media.
web.feat.img.7: Background removal - chroma-key out a single color such as a green screen.
web.feat.video.title: Video: Cuts Without Re-encoding
web.feat.video.1: Trim - cut one video or audio file the moment you click. No re-encoding by default, so exports are fast.
web.feat.video.2: Thumbnail - export any single frame as a PNG or JPG image.
web.feat.video.3: Compress - automatically adjust to a target size with minimal quality or FPS loss.
web.feat.video.4: Resize / rotate - by ratio or exact pixels, with presets one click away in the menu.
web.feat.video.5: Convert - between MP4, MOV, MKV, M4A, AVI, WEBM, FLV, and GIF.
web.feat.video.6: Audio extraction - pull the audio track out of any video.
web.feat.video.7: Quality and speed - switch codecs (H.264 / H.265 / VP9 / AV1) and hardware encoding (NVENC / Quick Sync / AMF) in settings.
web.feat.video.cap: Process a single clip or thousands of audio files in one go
web.feat.folder.title: Folders: All the Dirty Work of Tidying Up
web.feat.folder.1: Duplicate removal - delete files that match by size, hash, and bytes in bulk.
web.feat.folder.2: Empty folder cleanup - remove accumulated empty folders with one click.
web.feat.folder.3: Tree view - visualize the folder structure to make organizing easier.
web.feat.folder.4: Batch rename - rename all files inside a folder at once.
web.feat.folder.5: Analyze - visualize which files take up space and where duplicates hide.
web.feat.folder.6: Compress - bundle the folder into a ZIP / 7z / TAR / tar.gz archive.
web.feat.folder.7: Extract - unpack ZIP / 7z / TAR / tar.gz / RAR into a new folder.
web.feat.text.title: Text: CSV, JSON, PDF
web.feat.text.1: PDF - preview, merge multiple files, and export to PNG / JPG / TXT.
web.feat.text.2: Text - convert file types, change character encodings (UTF-8 / UTF-16 / Shift_JIS...), and switch line endings (CRLF / LF).
web.feat.text.3: JSON - beautify and reorder keys with rules.
web.feat.text.4: JAR - decompile in one click and export the source code to a new folder.
web.feat.text.cap: Preview, merge, and export PDFs with ease - no Adobe Acrobat Reader required.
web.table.caption: Supported conversions
web.arch.title: How It Works
web.arch.desc: A C++ shell extension renders the menu inside Explorer, while a .NET application handles the actual work.
web.arch.shell.d: The front end that renders the right-click menu inside Explorer. As a native Windows IContextMenu handler it stays lightweight and reads the selected file's info on the spot.
web.arch.shell.1: Runs as a standard Explorer menu
web.arch.shell.2: Dynamically builds menus per file type
web.arch.shell.3: Sits under "Show more options" on Windows 11
web.arch.proc.d: Handles the real work - conversion, compression, analysis - and settings management. Invoked from the shell extension via a launcher, it reports progress and results back.
web.arch.proc.1: FFmpeg, ImageMagick, PDFium, and more bundled
web.arch.proc.2: Shows a progress window. On failure or cancel, it aborts and automatically deletes files being created
web.arch.proc.3: Settings are stored in a JSON file under %APPDATA%
web.install.title: Installs in 3 Steps
web.step.1d: Download the latest Flect-Setup.exe from Releases. If .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is missing, the setup detects it and guides you through.
web.step.2d: Just run the downloaded installer - every conversion and analysis engine is bundled with it. Explorer may restart during setup, which is normal.
web.step.3d: Right-click a file and open "Show more options" to find the Flect menu. Tune menu items and compression presets in the settings app.
web.step.3note: Run reg add "HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\{86ca1aa0-34aa-4e8b-a509-50c905bae2a2}\InprocServer32" /f /ve in Command Prompt and restart Explorer to show Flect in the first-level context menu. To undo, delete the registry key and restart.
web.install.ps.title: Or Install from PowerShell
web.install.ps.desc: Paste this into PowerShell. It downloads the latest Setup from Releases, checks version and installs it silently. If the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is missing, it asks before installing that too.
web.reqs.title: System Requirements
web.reqs.2: .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (the installer will guide you if it's missing)
web.reqs.3: HEVC Video Extensions is only required for HEIC export: Microsoft Store.
web.reqs.4: JDK / JRE is only needed for JAR decompilation.
web.reqs.5: A Windows language pack is only needed for OCR.
web.reqs.note: Engines for images, video, PDF, and decompilation are all bundled. No extra downloads, no server transfers - everything runs locally.
web.pkg.title: For Developers
web.pkg.desc: Build with just a few PowerShell scripts.
web.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
web.faq.q1: The Flect menu is buried under "Show more options"
web.faq.a1: Developers can install the optional Windows 11 extension to add Flect directly to the modern menu. It is separate from the standard installer. Alternatively, switch the context menu back to the Windows 10 style and Flect appears directly in it. Run reg add "HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\{86ca1aa0-34aa-4e8b-a509-50c905bae2a2}\InprocServer32" /f /ve in Command Prompt and restart Explorer. This affects the whole system, so delete the key if you'd rather not keep it.
web.faq.a2: As new files next to the originals - nothing is modified or deleted. If a name already exists, a sequential number like (1) is added.
web.faq.a3: By default, deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, so yes. Only if you switch to permanent deletion in settings can they no longer be restored.
web.faq.a4: HEIC export requires Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions (reading doesn't). Flect can't bundle this codec, so it uses Windows' WIC encoder for HEIC export only.
web.faq.q5: OCR warns me about a missing language
web.faq.a5: Flect uses Windows' built-in OCR. Check installed languages under Settings → OCR, where adding a language pack is also guided. Language packs can be large, and adding one may require administrator rights.
web.faq.q6: Trimmed video starts a bit before the marked point
web.faq.a6: That's the result of not re-encoding. Video is stored by keyframes, and cutting by copy has to rewind to the nearest keyframe, which can shift the start by a few seconds. For precise cuts, switch Settings → Video → Trim to "Match the marked position" - it trades a bit of speed. The same trim is available for a single audio file and follows this setting.
web.faq.q7: Aaah! Too many items in the right-click menu!
web.faq.a7: Open the settings app and uncheck the items you want to hide under General → Right-Click Menu Items.
web.faq.a8: Uninstall like any other app from Windows Settings → Apps.
web.faq.a9: In %APPDATA%\Flect\settings.json. Some values needed by the Explorer menu itself are also stored in HKCU\Software\Flect. "Reset settings" clears both while keeping shell registration and learned encoder results.
web.faq.q10: My antivirus flags Flect as a virus
web.faq.a10:
Flect's installer and executables are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen and some antivirus products may warn about them or quarantine them as unknown software. This is a false positive caused by the missing signature, not by anything Flect does. An installer that bundles tools such as ffmpeg is also more likely to trip heuristic detection.

Flect is distributed only through GitHub Releases and the official site (flect.konayuki.xyz). Each release publishes the SHA-256 of its files, so you can compare it with your download to confirm it has not been altered. If the hashes match, choose More info and then Run anyway on the warning, or add Flect's install folder to your antivirus exclusions. You do not need to turn off your antivirus.
web.faq.foot: If your question isn't answered here, report it on GitHub Issues - attaching the activity log helps a lot.
web.final.word:
That one chore of file organizing,
reduced to a single right click.
